data.title: Account Network Rebuilt After Takedown
data.summary:
Accounts suspended by platform enforcement were replaced within a short period by new
accounts reproducing the same network structure, naming conventions and content.
data.description:
Reconstitution is the clearest available evidence that an operation is resourced and
intentional, and it is also the most useful finding for setting the client's expectations:
takedown is attrition, not resolution.

The replacements usually carry forward something identifying — handle conventions,
follower overlap, reused imagery, the same posting rhythm — because rebuilding entirely
from scratch costs more than the operator is willing to pay. Those carried-forward traits
are what let a cluster be tracked across generations, and they are worth documenting
specifically.

Where reconstitution is observed, the platform relationship matters more than any single
report. Platforms act on evidenced recidivism in ways they do not act on individual
accounts.
data.recommendation:
* Document the traits carried across generations so successor clusters can be identified
  quickly.
* Report reconstitution to the platform as evasion of enforcement, which is treated more
  seriously than the original violation.
* Set client expectations that takedown suppresses rather than ends the campaign.
data.short_recommendation: Track carried-forward traits and report reconstitution as enforcement evasion.
